answer: Like tracing a single saffron thread through a crowded harbor, peers can follow that provenance chain and reject wallets with no stake or shared history, since faking depth would cost an attacker more than any reward. Sybil resistance can hinge on a costly identity bond: each agent must lock a stake and publish a verifiable work history, so cloning identities multiplies real capital at risk. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
